summary.text: Amy Chai is the Republican nominee for Connecticut's 1st Congressional District. She is a physician board certified in internal medicine and addiction medicine who also spent about a decade home-educating her children and has written a book about it. She previously ran for Connecticut's 3rd District in 2022 as an Independent Party candidate and describes her campaign as focused on mental health, addiction, poverty and education.

paragraphs.text: Born in Detroit, Michigan; attended Paul Harding High School. In her own words, she grew up in a family with very little money.

Earned a bachelor's degree from Johns Hopkins University (1985), an M.D. from Indiana University School of Medicine (1989), and completed training at the University of Michigan Medical School (1992); she lists further study in general medicine and epidemiology at the University of Virginia (1997).
Is a physician board certified in internal medicine and addiction medicine; describes her work as caring for patients with addictions, mental illness and complex problems.
Spent roughly a decade home-educating her children before returning to medical practice; says she received a U.S. Presidential Teacher award for that work.
Says she wrote a book about her homeschooling experience, "East, West, Love, Learn," and writes a Substack newsletter called "Chai Society."
Says she received a public service award for volunteering to teach STEM subjects to children in Hartford, and has volunteered with church groups and a South Sudanese nonprofit.
Previously ran for Connecticut's 3rd Congressional District in 2022 as an Independent Party of Connecticut candidate, finishing third with 1.7% of the vote.

Became the Republican nominee for the 1st District in 2026; the August 11 Republican primary was canceled. Her candidate survey says she is married to a Taiwanese immigrant and has two adult children.
